scripts.dev: bun run check && BUN_RUNTIME_TRANSPILER_CACHE_PATH=0 bun --hot --no-clear-screen src/index.ts

simple-git-hooks.pre-commit: bun biome check --staged --write --no-errors-on-unmatched && bun run test
simple-git-hooks.pre-push: bun run type-check:fast && bun run test:e2e

rootFiles.CLAUDE.md: always-on agent rules, read at the start of every session
rootFiles.README.md: the front door, where a reader arrives before any directory
rootFiles.package.json: the manifest bun resolves from the root and nowhere else
rootFiles.bun.lock: the lockfile bun writes beside the manifest
rootFiles.bunfig.toml: bun's own configuration, read from the root
rootFiles.tsconfig.json: the compiler reads it from the root of the project
rootFiles.biome.json: biome resolves its configuration from the root
rootFiles.playwright.config.ts: playwright resolves its configuration from the root
rootFiles.build.ts: the production build script `bun run build` runs
rootFiles..gitignore: git reads it from the root, and it governs the whole tree
rootFiles..env.example: copied to `.env`, which tooling reads from the root
rootFiles.local.ini.example: copied to `local.ini`, the CouchDB config docker-compose mounts
rootFiles.Dockerfile: the build context's root is the directory holding it
rootFiles..dockerignore: read from the build context's root, beside the Dockerfile
rootFiles.docker-compose.yml: the deployment's project file, resolved from the root

src/api/config.ts biome-ignore.why: process.env['X'] is what noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature demands and useLiteralKeys rejects

src/index.ts biome-ignore.why: two: process.env['X'] is what noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature demands and useLiteralKeys rejects; one: the dev route table holds an HTMLBundle that prod's does not

src/app/components/Header.tsx @ts-expect.why: an SVG import, which tsc has no module declaration for

package.json biome-ignore.why: the approval keys in this object, which the scanner counts as suppressions

package.json @ts-expect-error.why: the approval keys in this object, which the scanner counts as suppressions
